title: Agent registry: which agents does your tenant have, and who can stop them?
summary: The registry controls, licensing conditions and operational limits are supported by Microsoft documentation. The User access API row needs a small clarification naming the request-body settings already explained below the table.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block reaches the organisation-wide blocking control.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... select an agent from the list of agents. ... immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks the selected package.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access controls which users or groups can access agents and plugins.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins. ... Select who can access agents and plugins within your organization.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply the User access setting using the request details below the table.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors ... An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.
claims.fix: Append to controls[1].note: 'Set mode to applyOnce and baseline.resources to microsoft.agent.useraccess, resourceVersion 1; properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory sets everyone or noOne.' The cited create reference and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources document these fields; the prose already gives them.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Agent management rules > Add rule opens creation of a bulk lifecycle rule.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agents > Settings > Agent management rules, and then select Add rule.

claims.claim: An API for configuring the Microsoft 365 admin center agent management rules is not documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: 'agent management rules Microsoft 365 Graph API lifecycle bulk rules create run'; '"agent management rules" "API" Graph PowerShell'. Read agent-settings, Package Management API overview and Graph search results; none documents automation of these admin-center rules.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All Agents > Connected platforms > Manage > + Connect a platform starts a platform connection.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Agents > All Agents. ... In the Connected platforms web part, select Manage. ... Select + Connect a platform.

claims.claim: An API for creating or synchronizing Connected platforms connections is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Agent 365 connected platforms connection sync agents Microsoft Graph API create synchronize'; '"connected platforms" "API" "sync" "Agent 365"'. Read connected-platforms, provider search excerpts and Package Management API overview; none gives a connection create or sync API.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Assign new owner reaches ownership reassignment.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... select an Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agent that you want to reassign. ... immediately under the agent name, select Assign new owner.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/reassign reassigns package ownership.
claims.quote: Reassign ownership of a Copilot package to a different user. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/reassign

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > Registry opens the tenant agent inventory.
claims.quote: Registry refers to the agent inventory under Agents > All agents > Registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages reads the tenant package inventory.
claims.quote: Retrieves a list of the packages available in the tenant. ... GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/copilot/admin/catalog/packages

claims.claim: The block API is a beta preview operation.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The block API requires delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All | Not available. ... Application | Not available. | Not available.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits: A block is per agent
claims.claim: Agent actions apply to the selected agent and should not be assumed to apply to its whole plugin package.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. If the agent is included in a plugin, don't assume the action also applies to the whole plugin package, its skills, shared MCP servers, or connections.

claims.claim: The User access UI offers All users, No users and Specific users or groups.
claims.quote: The setting has three options: ... All users ... No users ... Specific users or groups

claims.claim: All users is the default User access setting.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: User access API; Open questions
claims.claim: The TCM useraccess resource supports everyone and noOne rather than specific-user or group selections.
claims.quote: userAssignmentCategory | Write | String | Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. | everyone, noOne

claims.claim: Apply template is a one-time bulk operation, not a scheduled rule.
claims.quote: The Apply template action is a one-time bulk operation. It isn't a scheduled rule.

claims.claim: The Agent 365 AI administrator creates and manages the external platform connection.
claims.quote: The Agent 365 AI administrator creates and manages the connection in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The source-platform administrator supplies the source credentials.
claims.quote: The platform administrator creates the source-platform credentials, grants the required permissions, and enables platform-side telemetry when applicable.

claims.claim: Supported platform connections require key-based credentials.
claims.quote: Every currently supported platform requires a key-based credential, such as an API key, secret, or private key.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Governance controls: Preview; Open questions
claims.claim: The reassign API is documented under beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/reassign

claims.claim: The reassign request body sets userId to the new owner's user ID.
claims.quote: userId | String | Required. The user ID of the new package owner.

claims.claim: UI ownership reassignment is limited to shared Agent Builder and Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: You can only reassign ownership of shared agents for Agent Builder and Copilot Studio agents.

claims.claim: CopilotPackages.Read.All is the least-privileged permission for listing packages.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotPackages.Read.All | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All ... Application | CopilotPackages.Read.All | CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: The agent registry is the central Microsoft 365 admin center inventory of agents available to the tenant.
claims.quote: The agent registry in Microsoft 365 admin center provides a centralized view of all agents available for your organization.

claims.claim: The registry shows agent ownership.
claims.quote: For each agent, you can see who owns it, how much people use it, and whether it has any risks.

claims.claim: The registry shows agent risk signals.
claims.quote: Risk signals in the Agent Registry are a consolidated set of agent-related security detections that give IT administrators a single view of agent risks across their tenant.

claims.claim: Administrators can install agents through the registry.
claims.quote: Install and uninstall | Install an agent for users without requiring manual installation by end users.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Administrators can delete agents from the inventory.
claims.quote: When you delete an agent in the Microsoft 365 admin center, the agent is soft deleted.

claims.claim: The agent registry is a capability of Microsoft Agent 365.
claims.quote: A key capability within Microsoft Agent 365 is the agent registry

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Agent 365 as an observability platform giving one organisational view of Microsoft and other companies' agents.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 is the observability platform for AI. It gives you one view of the agents in your organization, including agents from Microsoft and from other companies.

claims.claim: The registry includes agents from Microsoft, partners and the organisation's own teams.
claims.quote: It includes agents from Microsoft, from partners, and from your own teams.

claims.claim: Microsoft agents are built and maintained by Microsoft.
claims.quote: Microsoft agents | Agents built and maintained by Microsoft.

claims.claim: External partner-built agents are built by trusted non-Microsoft developers for broader or public availability.
claims.quote: External partner-built agents | Agents built by trusted non-Microsoft developers and published for broader or public availability.

claims.claim: Published by your org means custom agents approved and published by the organisation, also called line-of-business agents.
claims.quote: Published by your org | Custom agents approved and published by your organization for broader use. These agents might be referred to as LOB (Line of Business) agents.

claims.claim: Shared by creator means agents created and shared by individual organisational users or developers, also called shared agents.
claims.quote: Shared by creator | Agents created and shared by individual users or developers at your organization. These agents are commonly referred to as Shared agents.

claims.where: What it is: How agents get in
claims.claim: The same Copilot Studio agent can have Shared by creator and Published by your org entries.
claims.quote: The same Copilot Studio agent (declarative or custom engine) can appear more than once in the registry with different publisher types, such as Shared by creator and Published by your org.

claims.where: What it is: How agents get in; Risks and limits: Duplicate-looking rows
claims.claim: Duplicate-looking entries are separate lifecycle and publisher records by design.
claims.quote: These duplicate-looking rows are expected and by design. They represent separate lifecycle and publisher records for the same underlying agent, not an inventory error.

claims.where: What it is: How agents get in; Risks and limits: Duplicate-looking rows
claims.claim: Removing one duplicate-looking entry does not remove the other.
claims.quote: Available admin actions differ by agent type and publisher state. ... Removing one entry doesn't remove the other.

claims.where: What it is: How agents get in
claims.claim: Add agent accepts an agent packaged in a ZIP file.
claims.quote: Add agent | Provides a method to upload an agent manifest file (.zip). ... To upload an agent, the agent must be contained in a ZIP packet file.

claims.where: What it is: How agents get in
claims.claim: Connected platforms connections allow Agent 365 to discover supported external agents and add them to the registry.
claims.quote: After you create a connection, Agent 365 can discover supported agents and add them to the Microsoft 365 agent registry.

claims.where: What it is: How agents get in
claims.claim: Amazon Bedrock is a supported connected platform.
claims.quote: Amazon Bedrock | Agents Classic and AgentCore | Yes | Yes

claims.where: What it is: How agents get in
claims.claim: Google Vertex AI is a supported connected platform.
claims.quote: Google Vertex AI | Vertex AI agents | Yes | Yes

claims.claim: The registry summarises the total number of tenant agents.
claims.quote: Total agents | The number of agents available in your organization's tenant.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: The registry summarises agents without owners.
claims.quote: Agents without owners | The number of agents that no longer have owners at your organization.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: The registry summarises unmanaged agents.
claims.quote: Unmanaged agents | The number of agents created or managed outside of Agent 365, without its risk protection and observability.

claims.claim: Unmanaged agents are agents created or managed outside Agent 365.
claims.quote: Unmanaged agents | The number of agents created or managed outside of Agent 365, without its risk protection and observability.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra's agent inventory focuses on agents with a Microsoft Entra Agent ID, whereas Agent 365 includes agents without one.
claims.quote: Identity administrators can see agents that have a Microsoft Entra Agent ID for viewing and managing them. The comprehensive agent inventory, including agents without a Microsoft Entra agent identity, is available in Agent 365.

claims.claim: Shared agents can become ownerless when their creator is deleted from the organisation.
claims.quote: Shared agents can become ownerless when you delete the user who created them from the organization.

claims.claim: Block restricts the selected agent across the organisation, subject to the host exceptions explained in Risks and limits.
claims.quote: Block and unblock | Restrict access to an agent across the organization, preventing any user from using it. ... blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: User access settings decide which organisational users can use agents and plugins.
claims.quote: While some users in your organization might have permission to install and use agents and plugins from the Agent Registry list, only the users or groups you select in this setting can use agents and plugins.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Viewing the inventory
claims.claim: Viewing all agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center does not require a specific licence.
claims.quote: Viewing all agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center doesn't require a specific license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Viewing the inventory
claims.claim: An appropriate role such as AI Reader or AI Administrator is required to view the inventory.
claims.quote: Administrators only need the appropriate role, such as AI Reader (recommended least-privilege role) or AI Administrator, to access the inventory view.

claims.claim: Viewing risk signals requires an E7 or A365 licence in the tenant.
claims.quote: Prerequisites for viewing risk signals ... Your tenant must have an E7 or A365 license.

claims.claim: Microsoft Agent 365 is licensed per user.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 is licensed on a per-user basis.

claims.claim: At least one user must have a qualifying Microsoft Agent 365 licence to enable Agent 365.
claims.quote: At least one user must be licensed with a qualifying Microsoft Agent 365 license to enable Agent 365.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E7 includes Microsoft Agent 365.
claims.quote: Microsoft Agent 365 is also included in Microsoft 365 (E7).

claims.claim: Microsoft's Agent 365 pages point readers to its plans and pricing.
claims.quote: For plans and pricing information, see Microsoft Agent 365: The Control Plane for Agents.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Connected platforms; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Collecting connected-platform telemetry can incur source-provider data access or query charges billed by that provider.
claims.quote: Retrieving agent telemetry from the connected platform might query the provider's own logging or data services (for example, Google BigQuery or Amazon S3) and can incur data access or query charges that the provider bills.

claims.claim: Entra security and governance controls for agents, such as Conditional Access, require appropriate Microsoft Entra Agent ID licensing.
claims.quote: Applying security and governance controls for agents, such as Conditional Access or identity governance policies, requires the appropriate licensing for Microsoft Entra Agent ID.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A block is per agent

claims.where: Risks and limits: Connected platforms sync by hand

claims.quote: Synchronization doesn't currently guarantee that an agent removed from the source platform is automatically removed from the Microsoft 365 agent registry. ... remove the agent from the registry manually if it's no longer needed.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Observability collection starts on

claims.quote: Agent observability data collection (preview) ... This feature is part of Frontier preview program.

claims.quote: A soft-deleted agent is unavailable to its maker and end users, but its properties and associated resources are retained for 30 days.

claims.claim: After ownership reassignment, the previous owner loses all access including read rights.
claims.quote: The following changes occur after owner reassignment: ... The previous owner loses all access, including read rights.

claims.claim: The documented TCM remediation and applyOnce preview is available only in the global service.
claims.quote: These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta. TCM is available only in the global service, not in national clouds.

claims.claim: Agent and plugin access controls which categories users can view and install from the catalog.
claims.quote: The Agent and plugin access setting controls which types of agents and plugins users can view and install from the agent catalog.

claims.claim: When Microsoft-built agent access is disabled, users still see those agents but cannot install them.
claims.quote: Users see agents and plugins built by Microsoft even if you disable the setting, but they can't install those agents and plugins.

claims.claim: Microsoft says use of beta APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Sync agents can be rerun before inventory reviews and after source-platform changes.
claims.quote: Re-run Sync agents after you add, update, or remove agents in the source platform, and before reviews that depend on current registry data.
